decisions.intent: Make export file overwrite atomic on the kernel side and report a localized save failure message instead of a raw error string.

preconditions: A desktop export copies a generated file from the export temp directory to a user-selected destination.
The destination may already exist, may be occupied by another process (Windows), or its parent directory may not exist yet.
stateTransitions: The kernel copies the export file to a temporary file in the destination directory, then atomically renames it over the destination.
The source file is locked for the duration of the copy; only regular files are accepted.
On the frontend, a save failure shows the localized exportFileSaveFailed message and logs the underlying error.
outputs: The destination is replaced atomically and the temporary .siyuan-export-*.tmp file is removed on both success and failure.
The user sees the localized export save failure message instead of an untranslated error string.
New i18n key exportFileSaveFailed exists in all 21 language files.
invariants: The export temp source path remains under the managed export base directory.
Encrypted managed export paths keep their existing box lock and DEK checks.
The existing filelock and logging semantics are preserved.
failures: A missing source, non-regular source, unreadable source, unwritable destination directory, or a destination that is a directory fails explicitly without leaving a temporary file behind.
A Windows destination occupied by another process fails without replacing the existing file.

notes: Ported with the local kernel api structure and ipcInvoke/siyuanI18n abstractions; kernel copy logic follows upstream copyExportFileToDestination, frontend failure message uses siyuanI18n.exportFileSaveFailed.

decisions.intent: Allow the user to reselect an export destination when the initial copy fails, instead of aborting the whole save flow.

preconditions: A desktop Electron export invokes saveExportFile and the user selects a destination via the native save dialog.
The kernel copy may fail (for example because the destination is currently in use).
stateTransitions: The save dialog is presented in a loop; a cancel hides all pending messages and returns without copying.
A failed copy shows a reusable localized error message and reopens the dialog with the previously selected path as the new default.
A successful copy breaks the loop, hides the progress and error messages, and shows the exported confirmation.
outputs: The user can correct the destination after a save failure without restarting the export flow.
Only one save error message is visible at a time (message ID is reused).
The exported success message appears only after the copy actually succeeds.
invariants: Cancel never issues a copy request.
The non-Electron branches (Android/iOS/Harmony/browser) keep their existing behavior.
The exported progress message is hidden exactly once on success.
failures: A final unexpected error shows the localized save failure message and returns; no partial copy is reported as success.
